Eiger, Mönch and Jungfrau peaks, Lauterbrunnen's 72 waterfalls, Wengen, Mürren and Lake Thun & Brienz.

Overview

Interlaken, Grindelwald & Jungfrau Region (Berner Oberland) is one of the essential stops in Switzerland, located in the Canton of Bern region. Eiger, Mönch and Jungfrau peaks, Lauterbrunnen's 72 waterfalls, Wengen, Mürren and Lake Thun & Brienz.

With direct connections via SBB CFF FFS & Panoramic Alpine Railways, Interlaken, Grindelwald & Jungfrau Region rewards a stay of 3–5 days so you can balance major landmarks with neighborhood cafés, markets, and easy half-day excursions.

RegionCanton of Bern
Best timeApr–Jun & Sep–Oct
Suggested stay3–5 days
Good forCanton of Bern, Culture & Sightseeing, Food & Dining, Rail Hub

Where to stay by budget

Budget

Well-connected hostels and guesthouses within a 10-minute walk of Interlaken, Grindelwald & Jungfrau Region's central station or metro lines.

Mid-range

Boutique 3-to-4-star hotels near the historic center and pedestrian promenade.

Luxury

Heritage 5-star grand hotels and design properties with concierge access and views.

Rough nightly ranges: hostels and capsule hotels often run a few thousand yen per person; business hotels commonly CHF 8,000–CHF 20,000 per room; upscale hotels and ryokan can be far higher, especially in peak seasons. See our accommodation guide.

Getting there

Interlaken, Grindelwald & Jungfrau Region is served by SBB CFF FFS & Panoramic Alpine Railways and intercity express trains as well as regional airport transfers. Book high-speed legs 2–6 weeks ahead for early-bird fares.

Getting around

The historic core of Interlaken, Grindelwald & Jungfrau Region is best explored on foot, supplemented by contactless tap-to-pay metro, tram, or bus lines.

Day trips & side trips

Scenic Regional Excursion from Interlaken, Grindelwald & Jungfrau Region

30–60 minutes by regional train into the surrounding Canton of Bern countryside and nearby historic towns.

Neighboring Heritage Town

Combine morning sightseeing with a long local lunch featuring Artisanal Canton of Bern Pastry & Wine.

Best time to visit

Spring (April–June) and autumn (September–October) bring mild walking weather and harvest festivals to Interlaken, Grindelwald & Jungfrau Region. Summer offers long daylight hours, while winter brings festive markets and lower hotel rates.

Local tips

  • Start at Interlaken, Grindelwald & Jungfrau Region Historic Center & Main Square before 9:00 AM to beat day-trip tour groups.
  • Use contactless credit cards or mobile transit passes on Interlaken, Grindelwald & Jungfrau Region buses, trams, and metro gates.
  • Order Traditional Interlaken, Grindelwald & Jungfrau Region House Specialty at lunch for the best value set menus.
